alex: Quick RFC follow-up re: iterator prefetch + transport adapters. I wrote a short note with api sketches and some operational clarifications. want povs before i edit the RFC.

maria: do we have to change public signatures? or can this be purely adapter-side behavior?

alex: adapter-only. public iterable APIs stay the same. transports may register an optional prefetch hook that negotiates a per-session window and atomicity.

jeff: sketch the handshake so i can reason about fallback and dedupe.

alex: handshake (high level):
- adapter.register(session_id, capabilities={prefetch:true, max_window:4, atomicity:"resumable"})
- coordinator.allocate(session_id, tokens=K)  # K <= max_window
- adapter.prefetch uses tokens; coordinator tracks reservations
Dedup rule: any returned page includes resume_token = server_token || epoch || checksum. adapters must drop duplicates by token.

sam: how do we bill or quota for reserved pages that are never consumed?

alex: proposal: reservations are soft. reserve bookkeeping increments reserved_slots metric but billing occurs only when page materializes and is handed to user. If eviction happens, no charge. Console shows reserved vs consumed.

natalie: backpressure: if consumer pulls slowly, prefetch must stall. Implementation: token-bucket per-session. tokens refilled as consumer advances; if tokens exhausted adapter stops prefetching.

maria: retries: prefetch errors shouldnt block current fetch. background retry with capped attempts. on final failure, iterator raises when consumer advances. keep a single logical RetryConfig on the call; adapters may apply lower caps for prefetch attempts.

jeff: operational: ensure monotonic fallback. if grpc prefetch returns page 5 and http later also returns 5, dedupe using full resume token. Also surface metrics: pending_prefetch, reserved_slots, prefetch_failures.

sam: for Go, be explicit about context cancellation: Pages(ctx, req...) returns (<-chan Page, <-chan error) and prefetch hook must respect ctx.Done().

natalie: UX suggestion: default disable_client_prefetch=false, but expose explicit_resume_only (or disable_client_prefetch) to force server-only progression. Default prefetch small for Hosted (1 slot), higher for Dedicated.

alex: security/consistency note: for private deployments, we can offer durable reservations (write-through) as an opt-in for teams that need auditability. otherwise reservations are ephemeral. add admin trace to list session reservations and lineage epochs.

maria: ok. can you add a small code example for TS + Python to the RFC showing no-arg pages() and how transport config opts in?

alex: yes. minimal snippets: 
```python
def pages(req, retry: RetryConfig|None=None) -> Iterator[Page]:
    ...
# transport config: client.connect(transport="grpc", prefetch={"enabled":True, "max_window":4})
```
```ts
function pages(req: Request, opts?: {retry?: RetryOpts}): AsyncIterable<Page> { /* unchanged */ }
// client.connect({transport:'grpc', prefetch:{enabled:true, maxWindow:4}})
```

sam: action items: 1) keep public API unchanged, 2) document reservation billing + metrics, 3) require resume token with epoch+checksum, 4) add admin trace + opt-in durable reservations, 5) make default prefetch conservative.

alex: i'll fold this into the RFC and ping for a 30m sync. thanks all. :thumbsup:
